_meta.description: Policy & fiscal forces acting on the universe — regime state (what the rules ARE right now), fiscal programs (who is paying whom), and levers to watch. Reconcile alongside the catalyst calendar; >60 days without reconciling = stale.

regimes.title: Export controls: tiered and whiplash-prone
regimes.state: Within twelve months Washington banned the H200, unbanned it (BIS rule effective Jan 16, 2026), then put a 25% tariff on it. Current shape: 'green-zone' chips (H20-class) flow freely, H200 sells under license + tariff, frontier GPUs stay banned. Jun 2026: BIS affirmed controls reach Chinese firms' overseas subsidiaries (closing the offshore loophole). Feb 2026: eight lawmakers pushed for a blanket WFE ban to China — entity-specific controls judged leaky. Jul 28 2026: the FCC opened a THIRD front — adding foreign-produced connected power inverters and advanced robotic devices to its Covered List (DA 26-786), which bars them from equipment authorisation and therefore from being imported or sold. Aug 4 2026 (Reuters): a parallel measure on Chinese optical modules is drafting. Officials hope to publish this year; it could still be modified or shelved.
regimes.watch: The regime changes with the political weather — that volatility, not any single rule, is the risk to price. NVDA/AMD China revenue swings on every revision; a blanket WFE ban would hit AMAT/LRCX/KLAC/8035.T's China backlogs. The newer worry is the instrument, not the target: see the production-origin regime below.

regimes.title: Materials leverage: suspended, not dismantled
regimes.state: China built a 12-category rare-earth/critical-materials control regime through 2025 (gallium/germanium ~98% refined share, tungsten hexafluoride, electronic-grade HF, 'look-through' end-user tracing — domestic-vs-export price gaps up to 100x). The Oct 2025 escalation was SUSPENDED for one year at the Xi-Trump truce — expiring Nov 10, 2026. Separate controls now aimed at Japan. Aug 5 2026 — MOFCOM answered the FCC robotics listing within a week: licence facilitation withdrawn for US-bound exports of controlled DRONES and their components (case-by-case review restored), CCC certification bodies barred from commissioning US labs for factory inspection, seven US entities blacklisted (one of them an FCC test lab), and a first-ever Article 41 Foreign Trade Law probe into imported printing and copying equipment. Note the choice of target: drones are the one mobile-robot category the FCC rule explicitly exempts.
regimes.watch: The Nov 10 expiry is a dated, binary event sitting under the robotics (magnets), optics (Ge/Ga) and fab-chemicals chains. Raw-materials names live in the Hard Assets sibling map — but the POLICY shock lands on this universe's act/opt/wfe verticals. The Aug 5 package also opened a quieter front — certification friction. Blocking CCC factory audits taxes every US hardware maker selling into China with delay rather than tariff, which is harder to price and harder to unwind.

regimes.title: Substitution mandates + Big Fund capital
regimes.state: State-directed decoupling: domestic-substitution quotas push SMIC/NAURA/Cambricon/Empyrean into captive demand regardless of economics, funded by Big Fund III (~$50B) plus provincial money. Antitrust probes of US chipmakers held as a retaliation card.
regimes.watch: Makes the china-localization cohort (30 tagged names) partly policy-driven rather than market-driven — treat their revenue 'demand' accordingly in conviction terms.

regimes.title: Production-origin bans, enforced through equipment authorisation
regimes.state: On Jul 28 2026 the FCC added two whole product classes to its Covered List by PLACE OF PRODUCTION rather than by company: foreign-produced connected power inverters, and foreign-produced advanced robotic devices (DA 26-786). 'Foreign-produced' means failing the Buy American domestic-end-product test (48 CFR 25.101(a)) — so a German, Japanese or Korean maker is caught on identical terms to a Chinese one, and a US brand manufacturing in Mexico is caught too. Covered gear cannot receive FCC equipment authorisation, which for anything carrying a radio is the gate to being imported, marketed or sold. Existing authorisations are grandfathered; the ban bites new models. The only exit is a Conditional Approval granted case-by-case by the Department of War (robots) or DoW/DHS (inverters), with no published decision timetable.
regimes.watch: This is the mechanism to track, not the two product classes. Export controls restrict what you may SELL abroad and entity lists name WHO is barred; this restricts what may be BUILT abroad and sold here, with a discretionary licence as the release valve. It is the same instrument now drafting for optical modules — which is why the transceiver measure should be read as a template rather than a one-off. For the map, the practical effect is that allied suppliers hold their position at the pleasure of a case-by-case exemption, and 'where is it manufactured' becomes a first-order question alongside 'who owns the technology'.

fiscal_programs.who: TSM (Arizona), INTC (18A buildout + high-NA), MU, 005930.KS (Taylor), AMKR-class OSAT reshoring — plus every fab-tool maker selling into subsidized shells (AMAT, LRCX, KLAC).
fiscal_programs.note: Reshoring changes geography, not chokepoint ownership — the same names win, in more expensive fabs. Watch a possible CHIPS 2.0 and datacenter-power permitting reform as the AI-era sequels.

fiscal_programs.who: 0981.HK SMIC, 002371.SZ NAURA, 688256.SH Cambricon, 301269.SZ Empyrean, 688234.SH SICC, CXMT (private) — the whole china-localization theme.
fiscal_programs.note: Capital without EUV access: expect capacity in mature nodes + brute-force advanced attempts. Deflationary for mature-node economics globally (our excluded lagging-edge names).

fiscal_programs.who: Rapidus (private, 2nm), TSM Kumamoto JV, 285A.T Kioxia, plus the equipment/materials complex (8035.T, Shin-Etsu, SUMCO) that a domestic fab base feeds.
fiscal_programs.note: Reinforces the japan-chokepoint theme — Japan pays to keep its materials/equipment moat physically at home.

fiscal_programs.who: ASML, AIXA.DE, SMHN.DE, SOI.PA, IFX.DE, ATS.VI, ENR.DE — the 9 records tagged eu-chips-act.
fiscal_programs.note: Pivot from mega-fab dreams to procurement + smaller-country niches — bullish the European equipment/substrate specialists rather than fab shells.

fiscal_programs.who: 000660.KS, 005930.KS + the Korean back-end cohort (Hanmi, Doosan Tesna, SEMCO, LG Innotek, Wonik IPS).
fiscal_programs.note: Underwrites the HBM capex race — and the 'Korea Unlocked' re-rating thesis.

fiscal_programs.who: Demand-side force: buys NVDA/AMD systems, Dell/SMCI/HPE integration, dci power/cooling — a second buyer class beside hyperscalers.
fiscal_programs.note: Fiscal money is less ROI-sensitive than corporate capex — it cushions the froth scenario where hyperscalers pause.

levers.l: LIVE — FCC Covered List now bars foreign-produced robots (Jul 28, 2026)
levers.d: Adopted, not proposed. Any ground-moving device over 4.4lb (with dock) that senses, connects and navigates cannot get FCC equipment authorisation unless the Department of War grants a Conditional Approval. Read the carve-outs before pricing it: industrial robotic ARMS, medical robots, vehicles and drones are explicitly excluded, so Fanuc, Yaskawa, ABB, KUKA/Midea, Estun and Doosan's cobots are untouched. What is caught is humanoids, quadrupeds and autonomous mobile robots — 9880.HK UBTech head-on, 277810.KQ Rainbow Robotics and TER's MiR unit on the same terms despite being allied, plus 1810.HK Xiaomi's consumer line. HSAI is hit second-hand through its customers' US market access. The asymmetry is the point: US-produced humanoids get a market cleared by rule, everyone else queues for a discretionary exemption.

levers.l: FCC optical-module ban — the scope question is the whole trade (drafting)
levers.d: Chinese vendors hold >50% of the global datacenter-transceiver market, InnoLight alone ~27% (Counterpoint); estimates of the supply cut run to 60%. The consensus trade is to buy the Western replacements — COHR, LITE, AAOI, FN, CIEN, NOK, MTSI, SMTC. Do not take that trade on the headline, because the draft has not resolved the one question that decides it: does the rule follow the COMPANY or the COUNTRY OF MANUFACTURE? Cignal AI, Aug 2026: 'unknown'. If it follows the company, InnoLight routes around it — it is already building in Thailand and Indonesia and sells non-Chinese output under the TeraHop brand — and the ban is largely cosmetic. If it follows the place of production, which is the test the FCC used for robots and inverters on Jul 28, then the replacements are caught too: Coherent manufactures in China, and Lumentum's North American assembly is ramping in THAILAND, as is Fabrinet's entire model. The only listed capacity that clears an origin test outright is AAOI's Sugar Land and Pearland build-out, live from summer 2026 — and Cignal judges AAOI too small to fill the gap. Both branches therefore end in shortage and cost inflation for the hyperscalers rather than clean substitution. Second-guessing the scope is the highest-value work on this lever; the beneficiary list is worthless until it resolves.

levers.l: The materials leg under every 'Western winner' still runs through China
levers.d: Worth holding against any policy-beneficiary trade in this map. OPTICS: every transceiver laser is built on an indium phosphide substrate, InP has been under Chinese export control since 2025, and it has no substitute at these speeds. Lumentum's CEO has called the InP shortage worse than the memory crunch; AXTI's backlog is >$100M into 2027, and AXTI itself produces in China under the same permit system. The May-Jun 2026 permit easing was selective and politically contingent, not structural. ROBOTICS: a US-built humanoid still needs NdFeB magnets, and the truce covering them expires Nov 10 2026. So a name can win the market-access argument by rule and still lose the input argument by permit. Raw-material depth lives in the Hard Assets sibling map — what belongs here is the conclusion: onshored assembly does not equal an onshored supply chain.
Renewal = status quo; lapse = magnets/Ga/Ge/chemicals shock into robotics, optics and fab chemicals. The single most dated policy risk on the board.

levers.l: Chinese WFE tools qualifying at Samsung and SK Hynix
levers.d: Reuters, Aug 4 2026: both Korean memory makers have been testing AMEC etch tools for their China fabs — begun ~2 years ago, aimed at SERVICING and upgrading existing lines rather than adding capacity, after Washington revoked their validated-end-user status in 2025 and replaced it with an annual licence. Small in units, large in meaning: qualification is the slow half of the WFE moat, and it is being done by the two customers whose sign-off other buyers copy. Deutsche Bank has NAURA, AMEC, Piotech and ACM Research each clearing $1B of revenue in 2026 and together taking 25-30% of China's ~$28B WFE market. This is the external bear case (see Thesis) arriving as an event rather than an opinion — watch whether qualification stays confined to China fabs.
If entity-lists give way to a China-wide equipment ban, AMAT/LRCX/KLAC/8035.T lose the remaining China backlog; ASML already effectively there on EUV.
Every H-series reclassification swings NVDA/AMD China revenue by $Bs and re-prices Cambricon/Huawei's captive market share in mirror image.
Chip/electronics tariffs would tax the Taiwan-assembled AI supply chain broadly — ODMs and packaged-silicon importers first.
The on/off lever on SNPS/CDNS China revenue (~10-15%) — historically toggled with little warning; Empyrean is the mirror trade.
Retaliation card against US chipmakers with China exposure (MU precedent 2023; NVDA probe on file).
